story_type: rocket plane explodes on the ground during an engine run with the pilot in the cockpit, historic color film
hook: The pilot was still in the cockpit when it blew apart.
narration: The pilot was still sitting in the cockpit when this rocket plane blew apart.
It was the X-15, built to reach six times the speed of sound.
In June 1960, test pilot Scott Crossfield sat strapped in for a ground run of its big new engine.
That engine could blast out nearly sixty thousand pounds of thrust.
Then came a call of malfunction, and the engine was shut down. [short pause] Seconds later, this.
Crossfield called it the biggest bang he had ever heard.
The blast threw the cockpit and the front tanks clear of most of the fire, and firemen moved in with foam.
Engineers traced it to a frozen pressure regulator and a faulty relief valve that let a tank burst.
outcome: Crossfield came out of it alive, and the system was redesigned and tested until engineers were sure the problem was solved.
preview_ok: Explosion shots are a near-white fireball filling the frame; the plane and stand show through the flames in each shot.
title: X-15 exploded with the pilot inside
question_comment: Would you have climbed back into the X-15 after that?

facts.claim: The X-15 program goal was six times the speed of sound
facts.source_quote: On the first try man and plane went 1/3 the way to the goal of six times the speed of sound.

facts.claim: The XLR-99 engine produced nearly 60,000 pounds of thrust
facts.source_quote: the XLR-99, a brute that would blast out nearly 60,000 pounds of thrust

facts.claim: Crossfield was the pilot and only eyewitness; biggest bang he ever heard
facts.source_quote: There was only one real observer, one eyewitness, the pilot, Scott Crossfield. Scott, what was your immediate reaction? Well, it was the biggest bang that I had ever heard.

facts.claim: The cockpit and tanks were blown out of the blaze; firemen used foam
facts.source_quote: the explosion blew the forward section in the tanks and the cockpit out of the blaze, or out of the major part of the blaze. And the firemen were right on their toes and they moved in to blanket the tanks and the fire area with foam.

facts.claim: Cause: frozen regulator and faulty relief valve
facts.source_quote: So, a frozen regulator, a faulty relief valve, and a high back pressure relief system had gotten together and we had wrecked an airplane.

facts.claim: Systems were redesigned and retested until the problem was solved
facts.source_quote: Weeks passed before we and everyone else were convinced that the problem was licked.
Since that ill fated day in June when the explosion ripped the number three ship in half

description:
An X-15 rocket plane explodes during a ground run of its new XLR-99 engine at Edwards Air Force Base in June 1960 with test pilot Scott Crossfield in the cockpit.
